preamble: Palatalization of the velar fricative [x] to the postalveolar [ʃ] before front vowels and *j. It is the outcome of *x in the Slavic first palatalization (*x > *xʲ > *š), which reverses the ruki retraction of *š to *x, and it recurs in Modern Greek dialects with 'heavy' velar fronting, such as Cypriot, Pontic and the Greek of Puglia, where /x/ before front vowels is [ʃ] rather than Standard Greek [ç].

examples.to: *šelmъ > Old Church Slavonic шлѣмъ šlěmŭ, Russian шлем

examples.note: *x became *š before the front vowel *ě, which then became *a after the new palatal.
Root-final *x became *š before the front vowel *i.
Cypriot has 'heavy' (palato-alveolar) velar fronting of /k ɡ x/, attested since at least the 15th century.
Fronting of [x] > [ʃ] is limited to a few lexical items in this dialect.

sources: Manolessou, I. & Pantelidis, N. (2012). Velar fronting in Modern Greek dialects. Modern Greek Dialects and Linguistic Theory 5(1), 272ff. https://pasithee.library.upatras.gr/mgdlt/article/download/2599/2836
